seoul-3-days.title: 3 Days in Seoul: The Perfect First-Timer Itinerary
seoul-3-days.metaTitle: 3 Days in Seoul: The Perfect Itinerary (2026)
seoul-3-days.sub: Palaces, hanok lanes, street food and skyline views — a relaxed but complete first visit to Seoul.
seoul-3-days.overview: This is the classic first-timer route: Old Seoul (palaces and hanok) on day one, modern Seoul and night views on day two, and a flexible day three for a day trip or your own picks. Everything is subway-connected — grab a T-money card and you're set.

stops.p: Gyeongbokgung Palace — arrive early, and wear a hanbok to get in free. Catch the changing-of-the-guard ceremony.
Wander Bukchon Hanok Village and the Samcheong-dong cafes, then Insadong for tea, galleries and souvenirs.
Dinner at Gwangjang Market (bindaetteok, mayak gimbap), one of Seoul's great old street-food markets.
Brunch and browsing in Hongdae — indie shops, cafes and buskers around the university.
Head to Namsan and ride up to N Seoul Tower for the city panorama; walk the leafy trails on the way.
Myeongdong for shopping, beauty stores and a second round of street food.

plan.area: Your pick — day trip or deep-dive

stops.p: Gangnam: COEX Starfield Library, K-Star Road in Apgujeong and upscale shopping.
A half-day DMZ tour to the inter-Korean border — book ahead (passport required).
Wind down at a Han River park (Yeouido) — grab convenience-store snacks and watch the bridges light up.

tips: Get a T-money card first — it covers subway, bus and most taxis.
Palaces close on different weekdays (Gyeongbokgung: Tuesdays) — check before you go.
Use Naver Map or KakaoMap for directions; Google Maps transit is limited in Korea.

korea-5-days.title: 5 Days in Korea: Seoul + Busan Itinerary
korea-5-days.metaTitle: 5 Days in Korea: Seoul + Busan Itinerary (2026)
korea-5-days.sub: The best of both cities — two days in Seoul, the KTX down to Busan, and the coast, temples and markets of the south.
korea-5-days.overview: Five days is enough for Korea's two biggest cities. Spend two days in Seoul, then take the KTX high-speed train (~2h40) to Busan for beaches, a hillside art village and Korea's best seafood, before heading back.

stops.p: Gyeongbokgung Palace + the changing of the guard (hanbok = free entry).
Bukchon Hanok Village and Insadong.
Myeongdong street food and shopping.
Hongdae cafes and shops.
N Seoul Tower for the skyline.
Gwangjang Market or a Han River park.
KTX from Seoul Station to Busan (~2h40). Book a seat ahead on weekends.
Haeundae Beach and the Blueline Park sky capsule.
Gwangalli Beach for the Gwangan Bridge light show.
Gamcheon Culture Village — the pastel hillside neighbourhood.
Jagalchi Fish Market and BIFF Square street food in Nampo-dong.
Haedong Yonggungsa, a rare seaside temple, at golden hour.
Last-minute Busan beach or cafe, then KTX back to Seoul (or fly home from Gimhae).
If flying from Incheon, allow time for the AREX/airport transfer.

tips: Book KTX seats in advance for weekends and holidays (Korail Talk app / letskorail.com).
Busan is spread out — its subway plus Kakao T taxis cover most of it.
Two nights in Seoul + two in Busan keeps you from over-packing/unpacking.

korea-7-days.title: 7 Days in Korea: Seoul, Busan & Jeju Itinerary
korea-7-days.metaTitle: 7 Days in Korea: Seoul, Busan & Jeju (2026)
korea-7-days.sub: The full loop — historic Seoul, coastal Busan and the volcanic island of Jeju, linked by KTX and a short flight.
korea-7-days.overview: A week lets you add Jeju, Korea's holiday island, to the Seoul–Busan route. Two days in Seoul, two in Busan, then a short flight to Jeju for volcanic peaks, waterfalls and beaches. Rent a car on Jeju — public transport is limited.

stops.p: Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon Hanok Village, Insadong, and Myeongdong in the evening.
Hongdae, N Seoul Tower and Gwangjang Market — or add a DMZ half-day tour.
KTX to Busan; Haeundae Beach, Blueline Park and the Gwangalli night view.
Gamcheon Culture Village, Jagalchi Market and Haedong Yonggungsa Temple.
Short flight from Gimhae (Busan) to Jeju; pick up a rental car.
Seongsan Ilchulbong (Sunrise Peak) and Seopjikoji on the east coast.
Dongmun Market in Jeju City for dinner.
Cheonjiyeon Waterfall, the Jusangjeolli cliffs and the Jungmun resort beaches around Seogwipo.
Hyeopjae Beach and Hallim Park on the west coast.
Return the car and fly out (Jeju → Seoul/Incheon for international connections).

tips: Rent a car on Jeju — buses are slow and sights are spread around the coast.
Jeju flights are frequent and cheap (one of the world's busiest routes from Seoul).
Check whether your international flight leaves from Incheon and leave a buffer to get there.
